https://thenewbev.com/program/august-1-d.description: In a hyper-violent dystopic metropolis, an elite law enforcement group acts as judge, jury, and executioner. And when veteran officer Judge Dredd (Karl Urban) and his young recruit (Olivia Thirlby) arrive at a 200-storey tower block to investigate a murder, they’ll find themselves in a ruthless battle with a vicious drug kingpin (Lena Headey) and her seemingly endless army of killers. Screenwriter Alex Garland adapts the legendary comic.

https://thenewbev.com/program/august-1-t.description: Danny DeVito and Billy Crystal star in a black comedy riff on Hitchcock’s Strangers on a Train ! Crystal plays a newly divorced sad sack bitter that his ex-wife stole his novel and turned it into her own bestseller. DeVito is the long-suffering momma’s boy eager to get out from his mother’s thumb. But when one suggests trading murders as the perfect alibi, the foul play will spin hilariously out of control. DeVito directs his first theatrical feature film, while director of photography Barry Sonnenfeld adds a stylish & energetic verve to the proceedings (the same year he also helmed Raising Arizona ). Plus, Anne Ramsey is unforgettable as DeVito’s domineering mother.

https://thenewbev.com/program/august-1-w.description: An animated coming of age classic from the beloved Studio Ghibli, featuring a funny, heartfelt screenplay by Hayao Miyazaki based on the original manga by Aoi Hiiragi. When a quiet, creative girl with dreams of becoming a writer looks carefully through her library books, she discovers they were all checked out previously by the same person, leading her on a life-changing quest that unlocks her talent & potential. Take Me Home, Country Roads.

https://thenewbev.com/program/august-10-.description: An idyllic summer town descends into madness when an ice cream man serves kids sweet delights with horrifying results. (The Horror Section)

https://thenewbev.com/program/august-11-.description: An idyllic summer town descends into madness when an ice cream man serves kids sweet delights with horrifying results. (The Horror Section)

https://thenewbev.com/program/august-12-.description: In this captivating and philosophical film directed by Louis Malle, actor and playwright Wallace Shawn sits down with his friend the theater director André Gregory at a restaurant on New York’s Upper West Side, and the pair proceed through an alternately whimsical and despairing confessional about love, death, money, and all the superstition in between. Playing variations on their own New York–honed personas, Shawn and Gregory, who also cowrote the screenplay, dive in with introspective intellectual gusto, and Malle captures it all with a delicate, artful detachment. A fascinating freeze-frame of cosmopolitan culture, My Dinner with André remains a unique work in cinema history. (Janus Films)

https://thenewbev.com/program/august-14-.description: Winner of 8 Academy Awards, including Best Actress and Best Director, director / choreographer Bob Fosse’s adaptation of the Broadway show is a stylish, big screen musical masterpiece. Set in 1931 Berlin, Cabaret chronicles young American Sally Bowles (Liza Minnelli) and her bohemian life as a performer at the Kit Kat Klub during the last days of the Weimar Republic, as well as her relationships with a reserved academic (Michael York) and a rich playboy (Helmut Griem). Minnelli is electric in her star-making role and a stellar Joel Grey shines in his Best Supporting Actor performance as the bawdy Master of Ceremonies.

Sir Lancelot (Robert Taylor) is sworn to serve King Arthur (Mel Ferrer), but his devotion to the queen (Ava Gardner) could provide fuel for their enemies to destroy Camelot.

https://thenewbev.com/program/august-22-.description: Documentary filmmaker Terry Zwigoff’s first fictional feature is a bitingly funny adaptation of Daniel Clowes’ famed underground comic. A sardonic Thora Birch and a young Scarlett Johansson are quintessential teenage outsiders adrift in post-high school ennui. But crossing paths with kindred spirit Seymour (Steve Buscemi) will change their friendship forever. Filled with a dream team supporting cast, Ghost World creates specific, believable people and all-too-relatable cringe-inducing laughs.

The sands will rise. The heavens will part. The power will be unleashed. Brendan Fraser & Rachel Weisz star in a rollicking, thrill-a-minute adventure that’s one of the most entertaining blockbusters of the ‘90s. When an American adventurer (Fraser) teams with an Egyptologist librarian (Weisz) and her brother (John Hannah) to uncover the lost City of the Dead, they’ll discover that disturbing the slumber of an ancient priest doomed for eternity could destroy the world.

H.G. Wells’ most famous and fantastic story rockets across the screen in one of the most celebrated science fiction films of all time! When a mysterious object lands in a small Southern California town, a Martian invasion unleashes a mighty panorama of earth-shaking fury. Genre icon producer George Pal presents a classic terror tale for the atomic age, a thrill-a-minute stunner featuring Oscar-winning visual effects, iconic leads in Gene Barry and Ann Robinson, a stellar Leith Stevens score, and costuming by Edith Head.

A heart-racing spy story by Alfred Hitchcock, The 39 Steps follows Richard Hannay (Robert Donat) as he stumbles upon a conspiracy that thrusts him into a hectic chase across the Scottish moors – a chase in which he is both the pursuer and the pursued – as well as into an unexpected romance with the cool Pamela (Madeline Carroll). This classic wrong-man thriller from the Master of Suspense anticipates the director’s most famous works (especially North by Northwest ), and remains one of his cleverest and most entertaining films. Christopher Lee, Britt Ekland, Maud Adams, and Hervé Villechaize co-star in this globetrotting action hit filmed across Thailand, Hong Kong, Macau, and beyond.

https://thenewbev.com/program/august-3-t.description: Gypo Nolan stumbles through a foggy Irish night, his brain pickled in whiskey and his soul tormented by shame and fear. Gypo is an informer, a turncoat who betrayed his friend to the British police for 20 pounds. Now he can’t spend the money fast enough – nor can he run from his treachery fast enough – as he brawls, brags, swaggers and lies his way toward his fate. John Ford earned his first Best Director Academy Award, and star Victor McLaglen took home a Best Actor statuette for this searing four-time Oscar winner set in 1922 Dublin. Timely in its exploration of the tortured netherworld of human guilt, The Informer is filmmaking for the ages. (Warner Bros)

The most controversial movie ever made has lost none of its unflinching power, a cruel cinematic landmark featuring special effects so realistic that director Ruggero Deodato was arrested on suspicion of murder.

Calling all animation aficionados! Join us for a celebration of the art and history of one of our favorite mediums with our monthly Cartoon Club! Enjoy a feature-length assemblage of classic shorts, including rare gems unearthed from the vaults and other animated antics lovingly assembled from our large archive of film treasures.

https://thenewbev.com/program/august-8-s.description: In the role he was born to play, Jack Black is Dewey Finn, a slacker guitar player still holding on to the dream of being a rock star. Due to a mix-up (and a low-level con), the wildly unqualified Dewey ends up substitute teacher in a prestigious elementary school. He recruits the bored prep school kids to form a new band, so these talented kids can rock the battle of the bands like it’s never been rocked before. This hilariously quoteable contemporary classic made Jack Black a superstar. And of course, it’s got a killer rock n rock soundtrack featuring songs from Led Zeppelin, Cream, T. Rex and the Black Keys, not to mention the original anthems performed by the kids themselves. Let’s get rockin!

https://thenewbev.com/program/july-27-ti.description: This in-name-only sequel to the first film – but peppered with much of the same cast – is an action-packed Hong Kong cop comedy. Captain Lam is nearing 40 and looking to accomplish something memorable before retiring. But first he’s gotta help find his nephew a suitable wife… while avoiding the deadly crosshairs of a dangerous smuggling ring. The Killer ’s Danny Lee headlines with martial arts superstar Conan Lee.

https://thenewbev.com/program/july-28-du.description: Meet Tip, Pam, Larry, Kit, Dusty, Sweets McGee and nameless, aimless more with young faces and old eyes. Meet them, but don’t get too attached. Because tomorrow some of them may not be alive. Most of the people who appear in his astonishing semi-documentary about the daily life of Los Angeles heroin abusers are real-life addicts, caught up in an endless cycle of stealing, hustling, jail time, shooting up, and coming down. Realistic and unapologetic, the film includes only a handful of actors, including Billy Grey ( Father Knows Best ) portraying a street-smart drug dealer. Directed by Floyd Mutrux ( American Hot Wax ), with graphic cinematography by William A. Fraker ( Bullitt ), Dusty and Sweets McGee is “a film in its own category. There are long stretches during which it’s hard to take your eyes off the screen” (Mick LaSalle, San Francisco Chronicle ). (Warner Bros)

https://thenewbev.com/program/july-31-ja.description: A stewardess, a gun runner, a bail bondsman, a federal agent, an ex-con and a stoned-out beach bunny are all on the trail of half-million dollars in Quentin Tarantino’s Jackie Brown , a mesmerizing, all-star adaptation of Elmore Leonard’s novel Rum Punch . But who’s getting played and who’s gonna make the big score?

https://thenewbev.com/program/september-.description: Joe and Angela’s marriage is on thin ice. When they invite their enigmatic upstairs neighbors for a dinner party, the night spirals into unexpected places. Have they reignited the spark or lit the match that burns it all down? (A24)

Michelangelo Antonioni’s 1960s panoramas of contemporary alienation were decade-defining artistic events, and Red Desert, his first color film, is perhaps his most epochal. This provocative look at the spiritual desolation of the technological age – about a disaffected woman, brilliantly portrayed by Antonioni muse Monica Vitti, wandering through a bleak industrial landscape beset by power plants and environmental toxins, and tentatively flirting with her husband’s coworker, played by Richard Harris – continues to keep viewers spellbound. With one startling, painterly composition after another – of abandoned fishing cottages, electrical towers, looming docked ships – Red Desert creates a nearly apocalyptic image of its time, and confirms Antonioni as cinema’s preeminent poet of the modern age. (Janus Films)
Her child is gone. Her team of assassins has betrayed her. Now snatch your Pussy Wagon keychains off the hook and join us as Uma Thurman’s The Bride sets out in her search of vengeance to Kill Bill .

Written and directed by Paul Thomas Anderson and nominated for three Academy Awards, Magnolia is a cinematic Rubik’s Cube of heightened realism and complexity, that ambitiously interweaves stories set in the San Fernando Valley – brought to life with an exceptional cast. Earl Partridge (Jason Robards) and Jimmy Gator (Philip Baker Hall) each carries with them a gnawing regret like the very cancer they are both fighting, while the majority of the rest of the cast deals with the scars inflicted upon them in their youth, as they head towards their own emotional unravelling. Anderson takes a cue from Newton’s Third Law of Motion, “For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction,” and begins to fashion his own law in Magnolia – “There are no coincidences” – as the late-great magician Ricky Jay so convincingly narrates, via the almost supernatural circumstances of seven deaths outlined in the film’s prologue: “This was not just a matter of chance. These strange things happen all the time.” Magnolia put an exclamation mark on 90’s cinema, finding its way into Ingmar Bergman’s “Favorite Films” and Roger Ebert’s “Great Movies List.”

Getting back was only the beginning. Now our time traveling teen (Michael J. Fox) and his eccentric mentor (Christopher Lloyd) will have to navigate multiple timelines if they’re going to set their past, present, and future straight. But small changes could have giant consequences, especially when big bully Biff Tannen (Thomas F. Wilson) is involved.

Hell hath no fury like a ’58 Plymouth. When a bullied teen buys a dilapidated automobile named Christine , he sets out to repair her to her former beauty. But this cursed car has a terrifying mind of its own. Stephen King’s classic novel comes to life in a chiller from director John Carpenter. How do you kill something that can’t possibly be alive?

Some secrets are too huge to hide. When a mysterious, metal-munching monster crash lands in 1957 Maine, a curious young boy will make a 50-foot friend. But as Cold War paranoia threatens to engulf the region, our 9-year-old hero will have to find a way to save his cosmic companion. Brad Bird’s beloved big screen fantasy is an emotionally complex and awe-inspiring animated stunner.

Those screw-loose Airplane! creators have done it again! Leslie Nielsen stars as Police Squad’s own granite-jawed, rock-brained cop Frank Drebin, who bumbles across a mind-control scheme to assassinate Queen Elizabeth. Priscilla Presley, O.J. Simpson, a stuffed beaver, two baseball teams and an odd assortment of others join the wacko goings-on and blow the laugh-o-meter to smithereens. (Paramount)

Simpson, a stuffed beaver, two baseball teams and an odd assortment of others join the wacko goings-on and blow the laugh-o-meter to smithereens. (Paramount)

There’s something going on at the local video arcade – something totally insane, outrageously hilarious, very sexy and thoroughly entertaining: the hit film Joysticks ! Will a local businessman (Joe Don Baker) succeed in shutting down this “den of juvenile delinquency” or will saner heads, faster fingers and shiny quarters prevail? Will leather-clad King Vidiot (Jon Gries) and his troupe of high-tech video addicts ever be satiated? Legendary exploitation filmmaker Greydon Clark distills everything great about the 80s (punks, nerds, valley girls, wild fashion, and Pac-Man) into one video game-fueled, late-night partyblast. Featuring extensive use of classic machines (Galaxian, Pole Position, Super Pac-Man, Satan’s Hollow), an all-time-great theme song and an epic battle against parental disapproval, this is a film for people totally into fun!

The first rule of Fight Club is: You do not talk about Fight Club . David Fincher’s stylized adaptation of the Chuck Palahniuk book is a darkly comic and intoxicatingly energetic screen thunderbolt, a visually striking, critically polarizing, and often misunderstood exploration of modern-day man, mischief, madness, mayhem and soap. Brad Pitt, Edward Norton, and Helena Bonham Carter turn in powerful performances, while the Dust Brothers provide a propulsive score.

Writer-director Michael Mann’s electrifying crime saga intertwines the fates of two disparate, desperate men in a taut cat-and-mouse thriller across the streets of Los Angeles. While an intelligent master criminal plans one last daring high-stakes heist, the investigating detective’s all-consuming obsession with the case threatens to engulf them both. Robert De Niro and Al Pacino sizzle in one of the great films of the ’90s.

We’re not rated X for nothin’, baby! Director Ralph Bakshi’s pushes the limits in his outrageous & groundbreaking feature length debut, a lewd & rude riot that helped shatter the notion of what animation could be. Adapted from the work of R. Crumb, this audaciously satirical adults-only fable follows a free-spirited anthropomorphic feline in a series of wild & debaucherous counter-culture adventures.

Three against the wilderness… nothing could stop them – only instinct to guide them across 200 perilous miles of Canadian wilderness! An unlikely trio – a labrador retriever, bull terrier, and Siamese cat – must traverse treacherous terrain and overcome dangerous obstacles in their incredible journey home in Walt Disney’s fantastic real-life animal adventure.

Joe and Angela’s marriage is on thin ice. When they invite their enigmatic upstairs neighbors for a dinner party, the night spirals into unexpected places. Have they reignited the spark or lit the match that burns it all down? (A24)

A criminal on the run conceals his identity by becoming Alonzo the Armless, a carnival act who uses his feet to throw knives. But when the daughter of the circus owner catches his eye, he’ll go to extreme measures to win her affections. Lon Chaney, Joan Crawford, and Norman Kerry star in a startling & unforgettable silent classic from Freaks director Tod Browning.

They transplanted a white bigot’s head onto a soul brother’s body! The doctor blew it – the most fantastic medical experiment of the age. And now, with the fights, the fuzz, the chicks and the choppers… man, they’re really in deeeeep trouble! Ray Milland and Rosey Grier star in a raucously entertaining grindhouse great directed by exploitation legend Lee Frost.

Academy Award® winner James Stewart (1940 Best Actor, The Philadelphia Story and 1985 Honorary Oscar®), Jean Arthur, Academy Award® winner Lionel Barrymore (1931 Best Actor, A Free Soul ) and Edward Arnold star in this classic screwball comedy. Based on the phenomenally successful Kaufman-Hart play, You Can’t Take It With You was directed by Frank Capra and won two Academy Awards® (1938 Best Picture, Best Director) and garnered five more nominations. It was Capra’s third Oscar® for directing. Arthur stars as Alice Sycamore, the stable family member of an offbeat clan of free spirits who falls for Stewart, the down-to-earth son of a snooty, wealthy family. Amidst a backdrop of confusion, the two very different families rediscover the simple joys of life. (Sony Pictures)

What’s your favorite scary movie? No one is safe when a group of teens are pitted against a masked murderer that tests their knowledge of horror movies. Director Wes Craven and screenwriter Kevin Williamson mix keenly self-aware wit with modern scares to reinvent the slasher mold and reinvigorate the genre for a new generation, launching a sensation with their smash hit Scream .

The Marx Brothers take on the highbrow with full comedic force in one of their most beloved classics! With non-stop zingers, antics, gags, and fabulous musical interludes, this laugh-a-moment adventure posits Groucho as Otis P. Driftwood, would-be manager and opera producer trying (with Chico and Harpo as co-conspiring con artist stowaways) to kick-start the burgeoning careers and love lives of two young performers, making big Broadway bucks doing it.

Fifty years ago, the Japanese Defense Forces killed Godzilla… or so they thought. When a series of terrifying natural disasters begin to plague Japan, including the inexplicable offshore sinking of a U.S. submarine, a mystic old man warns his nation that Godzilla has come back to destroy Japan as revenge for all the souls lost in the Pacific War. When mere military might cannot squash the monster, the mystic man awakens the Holy Beasts of Yamato – King Ghidorah, Mothra and Baragon, sleeping giants that protected Japan in ancient times. These untamed mammoth beasts take on Godzilla with frightening supernatural brute power that has been 2,000 years in the making. Tradition and technology collide in this chilling high-tech, cutting-edge fable. (Sony Pictures)

In director Wes Anderson’s offbeat adventure comedy, internationally renowned oceanographer Steve Zissou and his eccentric crew embark on an expedition to find the shark that killed his partner. Along the way, they’ll face pirates and personal difficulties, as well as a number of strange figures from Zissou’s past. The all-star cast includes Bill Murray, Owen Wilson, Anjelica Huston, Willem Dafoe, Jeff Goldblum, and more.

Audie Murphy stars in this action-packed western filled with adventure and romance. Clay O’Mara (Murphy) is out for revenge as he pursues the rustlers who murdered his father and brother. Along the way, he arrests and later befriends gunslinger Whitey Kincaid (Dan Duryea). Together, they face a gang of their enemies and dole out their own brand of justice. (Universal)

Made between Husbands and A Woman Under the Influence , John Cassavetes’ offbeat romantic fairy tale may be the director’s most accessible & charming movie. A quirky, joyous and punch-drunk love story, the film follows an unlikely, opposites-attract romance blossoming between museum curator Minnie (Gena Rowlands) and parking lot attendant Moskowitz (Seymour Cassel). It’s an acting tour de force with Timothy Carey, Val Avery, Cassavetes and his mother Katherine in key supporting roles.

Everyone’s looking for it and they’ll do anything to get it! The Maltese Falcon , that is. It’s not just the opulent treasure in the mind’s eye of every San Francisco low-life, it’s also one of the first shining examples of Hollywood noir, a stunningly confident directing debut for John Huston, and a sordid melodrama which transformed Humphrey Bogart from B-movie sideman to star romantic lead. Mary Astor co-stars as the hot-blooded but inscrutable femme fatale who drags hard-boiled private eye Sam Spade (Bogart) into the hunt for the Falcon. Peter Lorre and Sydney Greenstreet (in his Academy Award-nominated film debut!) round out the conspiratorial cast as dandy-gangsters with twisted loyalties. The paradigm for film noir to come, this loaded, sordid mystery gets right to the tragic truth about love and crime: “It’s the stuff that dreams are made of.”

Choose life. Choose a job. Choose a starter home. Choose dental insurance, leisure wear and matching luggage. Choose your future. But why would anyone want to do a thing like that? Director Danny Boyle’s electrifying look at the exhilarating highs and terrifying lows of the Edinburgh drug scene is daringly original, energetically stylish, and brutally funny, with a stellar ensemble including Ewan McGregor, Jonny Lee Miller, and Robert Carlyle, plus one of the most iconic soundtracks of the ‘90s.

The story of a rebel and his bike. In Tim Burton’s dynamite feature length directorial debut, Pee-wee Herman explodes to life in one of the most exciting, creatively colorful, constantly quotable and enduring comedies of the decade! When his fully customized, fire engine red bicycle is stolen, Pee-wee sets off on a Big Adventure to get it back, hitchhiking cross-country and encountering a quirky cast of new friends along the way.

People once believed that when someone dies, a crow carries their soul to the land of the dead. But sometimes, just sometimes, the crow can bring that soul back to put the wrong things right. The big screen goth fantasy update of James O’Barr’s comic follows a murdered musician resurrected to avenge his death and the killing of his fiancé. Featuring a soulful performance by the late Brandon Lee, stellar, rain-slicked cinematography by Dariusz Wolski, and a propulsive, chart-topping soundtrack featuring songs by The Cure, The Jesus and Mary Chain, Rage Against the Machine, Nine Inch Nails, Stone Temple Pilots, and more.

His whole life was a million-to-one shot. A Philadelphia fighter who never made the big time… he showed he could take on a challenge… and won something bigger than a championship bout. Legendarily holding onto the sale of his script until he was allowed to play the lead, Sylvester Stallone shines in his signature role as the underdog southpaw who gives it all he’s got when given the once-in-a-lifetime chance to face off against the world heavyweight champion. Talia Shire, Burt Young, Carl Weathers, and Burgess Meredith co-star.
